1	//! Named wire constants shared by every crate (CLAUDE.md §4, §6). Bounds
2	//! stay here so the worker, the CLI, and the action cannot disagree about a
3	//! limit by drifting copies. Every constant cites the reason for its value.
4	
5	/// The exact body of `GET /nix-cache-info`. Priority 30 sorts cachet ahead
6	/// of cache.nixos.org (priority 40) in a client's substituter order, and
7	/// WantMassQuery permits nix to batch narinfo lookups.
8	pub const NIX_CACHE_INFO: &str = "StoreDir: /nix/store\nWantMassQuery: 1\nPriority: 30\n";
9	
10	/// The nix base32 alphabet: lowercase, excluding e, o, u, and t. Store-path
11	/// hashes are 32 chars; NAR file hashes are 52.
12	pub const NIX_BASE32_ALPHABET: &str = "REDACTED";
13	
14	/// Store-path hashes carry exactly this many nix base32 characters.
15	pub const STORE_PATH_HASH_LENGTH: usize = 32;
16	
17	/// NAR file hashes carry exactly this many nix base32 characters.
18	pub const NAR_FILE_HASH_LENGTH: usize = 52;
19	
20	/// The store directory every cachet narinfo names.
21	pub const NIX_STORE_DIR: &str = "/nix/store";
22	
23	/// A store path's name half: letters, digits, and `+-._?=`. Nix admits
24	/// exactly this set, and it excludes `/`, which is what stops a name from
25	/// smuggling a path segment.
26	pub const STORE_PATH_NAME_PATTERN: &str = r"^[a-zA-Z0-9+._?=-]+$";
27	
28	/// The longest store path name cachet accepts. 211 matches nixpkgs'
29	/// longest known name plus headroom; nix itself never publishes longer.
30	pub const STORE_PATH_NAME_BYTES_MAX: usize = 211;
31	
32	/// The suffix identifying a narinfo object.
33	pub const NARINFO_KEY_SUFFIX: &str = ".narinfo";
34	
35	/// The prefix under which every NAR object lives.
36	pub const NAR_KEY_PREFIX: &str = "nar/";
37	
38	/// The compression suffixes nix appends to a NAR key, by `Compression`
39	/// field value. Read paths accept exactly this set; the signing path
40	/// accepts only `""` and `.zst`.
41	pub const NAR_SUFFIXES: [&str; 8] = ["", ".xz", ".zst", ".bz2", ".gz", ".br", ".lzip", ".lz4"];
42	
43	/// The longest legal key is well under 70 bytes; anything over 128 is
44	/// refused by a length comparison before any pattern scan runs.
45	pub const KEY_BYTES_MAX: usize = 128;
46	
47	/// A narinfo body larger than this is refused with body_too_large: narinfos
48	/// are a few hundred bytes in practice, so 64 KiB is generous headroom and
49	/// still a hard guard in front of the parser.
50	pub const NARINFO_BYTES_MAX: u64 = 65_536;
51	
52	/// A narinfo with more lines than this is refused: the parser's work stays
53	/// linear and bounded regardless of content.
54	pub const NARINFO_LINES_MAX: usize = 2_048;
55	
56	/// One narinfo may name at most this many references. Caps both the parse
57	/// and the closure walk's fan-out per node.
58	pub const NARINFO_REFERENCES_MAX: usize = 1_024;
59	
60	/// The roots (lease renewal) payload is at most this many bytes: it is a
61	/// lease, not a bulk upload channel.
62	pub const ROOTS_BODY_BYTES_MAX: u64 = 524_288;
63	
64	/// A roots payload carries at most this many store paths or installables,
65	/// matching the push pipeline's closure cap.
66	pub const ROOTS_PATHS_MAX: usize = 4_096;
67	
68	/// A probe payload is at most this many bytes: `PUSH_PATHS_MAX` hashes
69	/// serialize to ~600 KB, so 1 MiB is headroom, and the byte cap answers
70	/// before the parser runs. The entry cap itself is `PUSH_PATHS_MAX`
71	/// shared with the push pipeline: one number, one truth, both sides.
72	pub const PROBE_BODY_BYTES_MAX: u64 = 1_048_576;
73	
74	/// The collector enumerates at most this many project leases per run.
75	pub const ROOTS_PROJECTS_MAX: usize = 256;
76	
77	/// The Workers secret holding the Cloudflare API token the counter
78	/// route reads with.
79	///
80	/// Scoped to reading account analytics and nothing else: it cannot
81	/// touch R2, KV, Workers, or DNS. A deployment without it counts
82	/// normally and simply cannot report, because collecting and reporting
83	/// are separate powers and only one of them needs a credential.
84	pub const STATS_TOKEN_SECRET: &str = "CACHET_STATS_TOKEN";
85	
86	/// The account the counter route queries under.
87	pub const ACCOUNT_ID_VAR: &str = "CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID";
88	
89	/// The dataset name the deployment writes to and reads back.
90	pub const STATS_DATASET_VAR: &str = "CACHET_STATS_DATASET";
91	
92	/// The binding name of the dataset every counted thing is written to.
93	pub const STATS_BINDING: &str = "CACHET_EVENTS";
94	
95	/// Where the counter route sends its statement.
96	///
97	/// A variable rather than a constant for the same reason the JWKS and
98	/// GitHub API addresses are: the lane points it at a stub so the answer
99	/// path is exercised, and the address is transport configuration while
100	/// the token is what authorises the query. A deployment leaves it unset
101	/// and gets `STATS_API_DEFAULT`.
102	pub const STATS_API_URL_VAR: &str = "CACHET_STATS_API_URL";
103	
104	/// Cloudflare's SQL API, where an unconfigured deployment asks.
105	pub const STATS_API_DEFAULT: &str = "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4";
106	
107	/// The deployment's own name, which the console prints in its header so
108	/// two of them open side by side are told apart.
109	pub const DEPLOY_NAME_VAR: &str = "CACHET_DEPLOY_NAME";
110	
111	/// The collector's cron expression, so the console can count down to the
112	/// next run. The deploy program is the only thing that knows what
113	/// schedule the worker was created with.
114	pub const GC_CRON_VAR: &str = "CACHET_GC_CRON";
115	
116	/// A stylesheet the console loads for licensed faces. Unset by default,
117	/// and the repository ships neither the fonts nor an address for them.
118	pub const FONT_CSS_VAR: &str = "CACHET_FONT_CSS";
119	
120	/// The prefix every read credential this deployment issues carries. It
121	/// is what lets the read path tell an issued token from an OIDC token
122	/// and from a GitHub token without trying each verifier in turn.
123	pub const READ_TOKEN_PREFIX: &str = "cachet_";
124	
125	/// The body after the prefix: 32 random bytes, base64url without
126	/// padding. 256 bits is past guessing, and a fixed length makes the
127	/// grammar a length check rather than a parse.
128	pub const READ_TOKEN_BODY_LENGTH: usize = 43;
129	
130	/// Issued read tokens live under this KV prefix, keyed by the token's
131	/// SHA-256 so the stored form cannot be presented.
132	pub const READ_TOKEN_KEY_PREFIX: &str = "readtoken/";
133	
134	/// How early a stored GitHub token is renewed before it expires.
135	///
136	/// A token that lapses between the staleness check and the API call it
137	/// is about to make would read as a membership failure, which is a
138	/// person losing cache access for a reason that has nothing to do with
139	/// them. Five minutes is far more than the round trip needs.
140	pub const GITHUB_RENEW_SKEW_MS: u64 = 300_000;
141	
142	/// How long an issued read token is accepted.
143	///
144	/// This is the outer bound on a laptop credential's life, not the
145	/// revocation window. Membership is re-checked against GitHub on the
146	/// verdict cache's schedule, so someone who leaves the organisation
147	/// loses access within that TTL; this is what stops a credential nobody
148	/// has used in a month from living forever. Revoking sooner than either
149	/// is deleting the record.
150	pub const READ_TOKEN_TTL_MS: u64 = 30 * MILLIS_PER_DAY;
151	
152	/// An Authorization header longer than this is refused as malformed_auth:
153	/// JWTs run a few kilobytes, so 8 KiB is generous room while still a hard
154	/// guard in front of the parsers.
155	pub const AUTH_HEADER_BYTES_MAX: usize = 8_192;
156	
157	/// The nix `Compression` value narinfos default to when the field is
158	/// absent.
159	pub const DEFAULT_COMPRESSION: &str = "bzip2";
160	
161	/// The sentinel value for provenance fields missing from a lease: claims
162	/// old documents may predate, readable as absence rather than as truth.
163	pub const UNKNOWN_CLAIM: &str = "unknown";
164	
165	/// A project name is at most this long. GitHub caps an owner at 39
166	/// characters and a repository at 100, so 140 covers the longest
167	/// owner-repository default that can exist.
168	pub const PROJECT_NAME_BYTES_MAX: usize = 140;
169	
170	/// A project name: alphanumerics, dots, underscores, and dashes, starting
171	/// alphanumeric; never containing `..`.
172	pub const PROJECT_NAME_PATTERN: &str = r"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$";
173	
174	/// One lease document per project under this prefix.
175	pub const ROOTS_KEY_PREFIX: &str = "roots/";
176	
177	/// In-flight multipart bookkeeping lives under this prefix, unreachable
178	/// from any request by construction.
179	pub const UPLOADS_KEY_PREFIX: &str = "uploads/";
180	
181	/// The GC's per-run stage artifacts live under this prefix.
182	pub const GC_RUNS_KEY_PREFIX: &str = "gc-runs/";
183	
184	/// The GC's run reports live under this prefix.
185	pub const GC_REPORTS_KEY_PREFIX: &str = "gc-reports/";
186	
187	/// The edge-cache generation document's key.
188	pub const GENERATION_OBJECT_KEY: &str = "meta/generation";
189	
190	/// A stored NAR's measured facts live under the reserved meta prefix,
191	/// keyed by the NAR's own bucket key: `meta/nar/<hash>.nar.zst` records
192	/// what `nar/<hash>.nar.zst` measured when it landed.
193	pub const NAR_FACTS_KEY_PREFIX: &str = "meta/";
194	
195	/// A facts document is two hashes and two integers; anything approaching
196	/// this is not one, and the cap precedes the read.
197	pub const NAR_FACTS_BYTES_MAX: u64 = 512;
198	
199	/// A NAR write declares how many bytes its frame decodes to, and the
200	/// decoder is bounded by that declaration. This is the ceiling on the
201	/// declaration itself: no single store path decompresses past it, and the
202	/// bound has to exist before the decode starts or it is not a bound.
203	pub const NAR_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES_MAX: u64 = 68_719_476_736;
204	
205	/// The decoder is bounded a second time, by how far the stored bytes may
206	/// expand. A declaration is attacker-chosen, so on its own it lets a tiny
207	/// upload ask for an enormous decode; pairing it with a ratio means a
208	/// compression bomb can only spend CPU in proportion to the bytes it
209	/// actually uploaded. Real NARs of ordinary store paths land near 3x and
210	/// even a tree of mostly zeroes stays well under this.
211	pub const NAR_EXPANSION_RATIO_MAX: u64 = 200;
212	
213	/// A well-formed generation document is under a hundred bytes; anything
214	/// approaching 256 is corrupt, and the read path bypasses the edge cache
215	/// rather than trusting it.
216	pub const GENERATION_DOCUMENT_BYTES_MAX: u64 = 256;
217	
218	/// The internal prefixes that requests can never address. Key validation
219	/// makes these unreachable from a request; the sweep's candidate filter
220	/// refuses them a second time, because deletion is unrecoverable.
221	pub const RESERVED_KEY_PREFIXES: [&str; 5] = [
222	    ROOTS_KEY_PREFIX,
223	    UPLOADS_KEY_PREFIX,
224	    GC_RUNS_KEY_PREFIX,
225	    GC_REPORTS_KEY_PREFIX,
226	    "meta/",
227	];
228	
229	/// Single-shot NAR PUT refuses bodies larger than this with body_too_large:
230	/// 90 MiB of headroom under Cloudflare's 100 MB edge request cap. Larger
231	/// NARs use the multipart routes.
232	pub const UPLOAD_SINGLE_MAX_BYTES: u64 = 94_371_800;
233	
234	/// A multipart completion body: 1000 parts at 256 bytes each is room to
235	/// spare, and the cap exists so the parser's bound precedes the read.
236	pub const COMPLETE_BODY_BYTES_MAX: u64 = 262_144;
237	
238	/// An upload bookkeeping record: four small fields; anything larger is
239	/// not one.
240	pub const UPLOAD_RECORD_BYTES_MAX: u64 = 1_024;
241	
242	/// Every multipart part except the last is exactly this size; the last is
243	/// the declared remainder.
244	pub const UPLOAD_PART_BYTES: u64 = 67_108_864;
245	
246	/// The multipart protocol rejects a plan with more than this many parts.
247	pub const MULTIPART_PARTS_MAX: u64 = 1_000;
248	
249	/// The push pipeline refuses closures adding more than this many store
250	/// paths. The guard's target is the missing-snapshot disaster (a before-set
251	/// that died, making the whole store one diff), not honest cold closures:
252	/// a fresh runner's devshell plus build closure legitimately lands in the
253	/// thousands, so the cap sits well above any first push and far below the
254	/// upload-everything shape.
255	pub const PUSH_PATHS_MAX: u64 = 16_384;
256	
257	/// An in-flight upload older than this is aborted: a week is far past any
258	/// honest client's retry window.
259	pub const UPLOAD_STALE_MAX_MS: u64 = 7 * MILLIS_PER_DAY;
260	
261	/// A lease renewed longer ago than this no longer protects its closure.
262	pub const LEASE_RETENTION_MS: u64 = 30 * MILLIS_PER_DAY;
263	
264	/// An unmarked object younger than the grace window survives the sweep:
265	/// in-flight writes and just-missed leases get one collection cycle to
266	/// settle.
267	pub const GRACE_WINDOW_MS: u64 = 14 * MILLIS_PER_DAY;
268	
269	/// The closure walk refuses to grow past this many visited paths, which
270	/// also bounds narinfo reads per run.
271	pub const CLOSURE_WALK_PATHS_MAX: usize = 100_000;
272	
273	/// GC run artifacts older than this are pruned; reports keep forever.
274	pub const GC_RUNS_RETENTION_MS: u64 = 30 * MILLIS_PER_DAY;
275	
276	/// Binding operations one GC invocation may spend before it hands the run
277	/// to the next tick: list pages, reads, puts, and delete batches count one
278	/// each.
279	pub const GC_OP_BUDGET: u64 = 900;
280	
281	/// Wall time one invocation may use before handing off, in milliseconds.
282	/// The scheduled-event ceiling is fifteen minutes and the margin absorbs
283	/// the final stage's writes.
284	pub const GC_HEADROOM_MS: u64 = 13 * 60 * 1_000;
285	
286	/// Run entries per gc-runs listing page: an admin page is a bounded read,
287	/// and deeper history pages through.
288	pub const GC_RUNS_PAGE_LIMIT: usize = 100;
289	
290	/// The index key the latest completed report's copy lives under, so the
291	/// stats endpoint answers from one read instead of a listing scan.
292	pub const GC_LATEST_REPORT_KEY: &str = "gc-reports/latest.json";
293	
294	/// Keys per deletion call: one batch is one binding operation, and the
295	/// batch shape is what keeps a 900-operation tick honest about real
296	/// deletions.
297	pub const GC_DELETE_BATCH: usize = 128;
298	
299	/// The run cursor's bucket key, inside the reserved prefix: the sweep
300	/// grammar and every request path already refuse it.
301	pub const GC_CURSOR_OBJECT_KEY: &str = "meta/gc-cursor";
302	
303	/// GitHub rotates its JWKS on its own schedule; ten minutes bounds our
304	/// staleness.
305	pub const JWKS_CACHE_TTL_MS: u64 = 600_000;
306	
307	/// Clock-skew tolerated on OIDC times, in milliseconds: five seconds
308	/// absorbs CAQ Runner clock drift without widening the replay window
309	/// materially.
310	pub const OIDC_CLOCK_TOLERANCE_MS: u64 = 5_000;
311	
312	/// A configuration may name at most this many GitHub orgs. More is far more
313	/// likely a delimiter mistake than a decision.
314	pub const ACCEPTED_ORGS_MAX: usize = 8;
315	
316	/// The verdict-cache lifetime for an allowed GitHub token: revoking a
317	/// laptop credential converges within this window.
318	pub const VERDICT_ALLOW_TTL_MS: u64 = 600_000;
319	
320	/// The verdict-cache lifetime for a denied GitHub token: membership grants
321	/// converge quickly without hammering the GitHub API.
322	pub const VERDICT_DENY_TTL_MS: u64 = 60_000;
323	
324	/// An OAuth state token lives this long: long enough for a human to finish
325	/// the GitHub prompt, short enough to bound replay.
326	pub const OAUTH_STATE_TTL_MS: u64 = 600_000;
327	
328	/// A browser session lives this long from its creation.
329	pub const SESSION_TTL_MS: u64 = 14 * MILLIS_PER_DAY;
330	
331	/// Objects per bucket-listing page: a parametric ceiling, not a knob.
332	pub const BUCKET_LIST_PAGE_LIMIT: usize = 1_000;
333	
334	/// The KV prefix under which GitHub-token verdicts live:
335	/// `ghverdict/{sha256}`.
336	pub const VERDICT_KEY_PREFIX: &str = "ghverdict/";
337	
338	/// The KV prefix under which browser sessions live: `sess/{id}`.
339	pub const SESSION_KEY_PREFIX: &str = "sess/";
340	
341	/// The KV prefix for OAuth state tickets: `oauth-state/{state}`.
342	pub const OAUTH_STATE_KEY_PREFIX: &str = "oauth-state/";
343	
344	/// The session cookie's name.
345	pub const SESSION_COOKIE_NAME: &str = "cachet_session";
346	
347	/// Milliseconds in a day, the unit conversion used by the retention
348	/// constants.
349	pub const MILLIS_PER_DAY: u64 = 86_400_000;
350	
351	/// Negative answers to the edge cache last this long: a missing narinfo is
352	/// usually being written this second.
353	pub const EDGE_NEGATIVE_TTL_SECONDS: u32 = 30;
354	
355	/// The generation document's own edge TTL: the staleness bound after a
356	/// destructive sweep.
357	pub const GENERATION_EDGE_TTL_SECONDS: u32 = 60;
358	
359	/// Positive edge-cache lifetime for cache objects: thirty days, immutable,
360	/// because an object under a content-derived key never changes.
361	pub const OBJECT_EDGE_TTL_SECONDS: u32 = 2_592_000;
362	
363	/// Objects larger than this stream without touching the edge cache: R2
364	/// streams them fine, and one early-release closure would evict everything
365	/// worth keeping.
366	pub const EDGE_CACHE_SIZE_CAP_BYTES: u64 = 512 * 1024 * 1024;
367	
368	/// The synthetic origin every edge-cache key is built under. The Cache API
369	/// keys on URLs, and `.invalid` is reserved by RFC 2606, so nothing here
370	/// can ever become a real request.
371	pub const EDGE_CACHE_KEY_ORIGIN: &str = "https://cachet-edge.invalid";
372	
373	/// The `/nix-cache-info` body changes with configuration, so its edge
374	/// lifetime is short: five minutes.
375	pub const CACHE_INFO_EDGE_TTL_SECONDS: u32 = 300;
376	
377	/// The content type nix expects for a narinfo.
378	pub const NARINFO_CONTENT_TYPE: &str = "text/x-nix-narinfo";
379	
380	/// The content type nix expects for a NAR object.
381	pub const NAR_CONTENT_TYPE: &str = "application/x-nix-nar";
382	
383	/// The content type nix expects for `/nix-cache-info`.
384	pub const CACHE_INFO_CONTENT_TYPE: &str = "text/x-nix-cache-info";
385	
386	/// The content type of an RFC 9457 problem document.
387	pub const PROBLEM_CONTENT_TYPE: &str = "application/problem+json";
388	
389	/// The OIDC issuer's JWKS document for verification of GitHub Actions
390	/// tokens. `CACHET_JWKS_URL` overrides it only in the lanes and for
391	/// issuers that are not github.com.
392	pub const JWKS_URL_DEFAULT: &str = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com/.well-known/jwks";
393	
394	/// The GitHub REST API root the verdict path and OAuth flows call.
395	/// `CACHET_GITHUB_API_URL` overrides it for the stub server in the lanes.
396	pub const GITHUB_API_URL_DEFAULT: &str = "https://api.github.com";
397	
398	/// The GitHub web origin the OAuth exchange posts to. The device flow and
399	/// the authorize redirect live on the same origin by construction;
400	/// `CACHET_GITHUB_WEB_URL` overrides it for the stub server in the lanes.
401	pub const GITHUB_WEB_URL_DEFAULT: &str = "https://github.com";
402	
403	/// An explicitly set value wins; an absent or blank value reads as the
404	/// default. This is the whole override rule the worker's outbound-URL
405	/// reads share, kept in one place so no call site invents its own
406	/// interpretation of an empty string.
407	pub fn override_or<'a>(value: Option<&'a str>, default: &'a str) -> &'a str {
408	    value.filter(|v| !v.trim().is_empty()).unwrap_or(default)
409	}
410	
411	#[cfg(test)]
412	mod tests {
413	    use super::*;
414	
415	    #[test]
416	    fn absent_answer_is_the_default() {
417	        assert_eq!(override_or(None, JWKS_URL_DEFAULT), JWKS_URL_DEFAULT);
418	    }
419	
420	    #[test]
421	    fn blank_answers_read_as_absent() {
422	        assert_eq!(override_or(Some(""), JWKS_URL_DEFAULT), JWKS_URL_DEFAULT);
423	        assert_eq!(
424	            override_or(Some("  "), GITHUB_API_URL_DEFAULT),
425	            GITHUB_API_URL_DEFAULT
426	        );
427	    }
428	
429	    #[test]
430	    fn a_set_value_wins() {
431	        let stub = "http://127.0.0.1:9/jwks";
432	        assert_eq!(override_or(Some(stub), JWKS_URL_DEFAULT), stub);
433	    }
434	}

# Every recipe is a thin alias over a flake output; the build logic lives in
# the flake, never here. `just check` is the pre-push parity verb: green
# locally means green in CI, because CI runs the same verbs.

sys := `nix eval --impure --raw --expr 'builtins.currentSystem'`

default: check

# the pre-push parity verb: every gate, one to one with the CI jobs
check:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    gates="$(nix eval --json '.#checks.{{ sys }}' --apply 'builtins.attrNames' | jq -r '.[] | ".#checks.{{ sys }}." + .')"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    nix build -L --keep-going $gates
    just deny
    just kani
    just wasm
    just clippy-wasm
    just wasm-hygiene
    just openapi-check

# format the tree
fmt:
    nix fmt

# check formatting
fmt-check:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.fmt'

# the workspace lint gate
clippy:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.clippy'

# the unit lane
unit:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.unit'

# the property lane
property:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.property'

# the golden lane
golden:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.golden'

# the kani lane; impure: the pinned verifier and its toolchain install under the user
kani crate="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    # why: kani-verifier is not packaged in nixpkgs; its pinned install and
    # toolchain download live outside the dev shell, like cargo deny.
    export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
    command -v cargo-kani >/dev/null 2>&1 || cargo install --locked kani-verifier@0.67.0
    cargo kani setup
    if [ -n "{{ crate }}" ]; then
        cargo kani -p "{{ crate }}"
    else
        for c in $(bash scripts/list-kani-crates.sh); do cargo kani -p "$c"; done
    fi

# the CLAUDE.md manifest bijection
doc-manifest:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.doc-manifest'

# the lane bijection
lane-manifest:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.lane-manifest'

# the workflow lint
actionlint:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.actionlint'

# the shell lint
scripts:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.scripts'

# the impure gate: cargo deny fetches the advisory database
deny:
    cargo deny check

# regenerate docs/openapi.yaml from the route descriptors
openapi:
    cargo run -p cachet-api --features yaml-export --bin openapi > docs/openapi.yaml

# the OpenAPI bijection: descriptors against the committed document
openapi-check:
    bash scripts/check-openapi-drift.sh

# build the deployable worker bundle with worker-build, then stamp the JS
# loader with the wasm's hash: deploy-time drift detection hashes the
# entry, whose text worker-build emits identically on every build — the
# stamp is how wasm-only changes still read as a change (ADR 0009).
wasm:
    # The commit the bundle was built from, stamped into the binary so the
    # console's header names it. A build outside a git tree leaves it
    # empty, and the worker then says nothing rather than naming a commit
    # it was not built from.
    cd crates/cachet-worker && CACHET_BUILD_SHA="$(git rev-parse --short=6 HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo '')" worker-build --profile worker
    printf '// cachet-bundle-sha256: %s\n' "$(openssl dgst -sha256 -r crates/cachet-worker/build/index_bg.wasm | cut -d' ' -f1)" >> crates/cachet-worker/build/index.js

# build the browser console into web/dist, which the deploy uploads as
# the worker's static assets (ADR 0014)
web:
    cd web && bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run build

# the console lane: the console's pure derivations and its presentational
# components, under vitest (docs/testing/console.md)
console:
    cd web && bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run typecheck && bun run test

# the workerd lane: the built worker under wrangler dev --local, real R2
# and Cache API semantics, asserted over real HTTP; the CLI binary rides
# the same lane, driven by the end-to-end push scenario
workerd: wasm
    cargo build -p cachet-cli
    node workerd/check.mjs fixtures/nix-signed

# the shipped-artifact hygiene gate: no banned runtimes, no secret-shaped strings
wasm-hygiene:
    bash scripts/check-wasm-hygiene.sh

# the worker crate's own lint pass, on its production target (the host
# clippy gate excludes it because it is wasm32-only)
clippy-wasm:
    cargo clippy -p cachet-worker --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --all-features -- --deny warnings

# deploy one stage end to end: build the bundle, source the stage's env
# file when present, run the alchemy stack. The operator's two secrets and
# the CACHET_DEPLOY_* set come from infra/.env.<stage> or the environment.
deploy stage: wasm web
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cd infra
    bun install --frozen-lockfile --silent
    if [ -f ".env.{{ stage }}" ]; then
        set -a
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        . ".env.{{ stage }}"
        set +a
    fi
    # why: alchemy asks before it changes anything, and a run with no
    # terminal cannot answer, so every CI deploy stopped at the prompt
    # with "Non-interactive terminal detected". Approving on behalf of a
    # run that has no way to be asked is not a decision being taken away
    # from anyone: it is the only answer available. A terminal still gets
    # the prompt, which is where a human is present to read the plan.
    approve=()
    if [ ! -t 0 ]; then
        approve=(--yes)
    fi
    # why: the output is inspected, not just the exit status. alchemy
    # answers its own refusal with a zero exit, so a deploy that printed
    # its plan and applied none of it reported success: staging went green
    # for days while running whatever it had before, and the integration
    # lane behind it tested that stale worker and passed. A deploy that
    # deploys nothing has to be red.
    log="$(mktemp)"
    trap 'rm -f "${log}"' EXIT
    set +e
    bun run deploy --stage "{{ stage }}" "${approve[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "${log}"
    status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
    set -e
    if [ "${status}" -ne 0 ]; then
        exit "${status}"
    fi
    if grep -q "Non-interactive terminal detected" "${log}"; then
        echo "cachet: alchemy printed its plan and applied none of it." >&2
        echo "  The deployment is unchanged. Nothing here can answer its prompt," >&2
        echo "  so this run cannot deploy; it must not report that it did." >&2
        exit 1
    fi

# tear one stage down; alchemy confirms before deleting anything
destroy stage:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cd infra
    if [ -f ".env.{{ stage }}" ]; then
        set -a
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        . ".env.{{ stage }}"
        set +a
    fi
    bun run destroy --stage "{{ stage }}"

# the first-run walkthrough: writes infra/.env.production and prints the
# checklists for the GitHub and Cloudflare sides
bootstrap *args:
    bash scripts/bootstrap.sh {{ args }}

# the integration lane: the live round trip against a deployment
integration:
    bash scripts/integration.sh

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The OpenAPI bijection: cachet-api's route descriptors against the
# committed docs/openapi.yaml, which is what the worker serves. This script
# regenerates the document and fails the build on any drift, because the
# served bytes and the code must be one fact (CLAUDE.md §0).
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="${1:-.}"
cd "$ROOT"

regenerated="$(mktemp -t cachet-openapi.XXXXXX)"
trap 'rm -f "$regenerated"' EXIT

cargo run --quiet -p cachet-api --features yaml-export --bin openapi >"$regenerated"

if ! cmp -s docs/openapi.yaml "$regenerated"; then
  echo "docs/openapi.yaml drifts from the route descriptors."
  echo "Regenerate it: nix develop --command just openapi"
  diff -u docs/openapi.yaml "$regenerated" | head -50 || true
  exit 1
fi

echo "openapi.yaml is in step with the code."

2	//! The binding roster: every name a deployment's configuration uses, in
3	//! one place.
4	//!
5	//! CLAUDE.md §7 forbids hand-maintained lists because they drift
6	//! silently, and this list had drifted into four homes before this
7	//! module existed: `sesame-worker`'s config parser, `wrangler.toml`,
8	//! `image/serve.mjs`, and `workerd/rig.ts`. A name added to one and
9	//! missed in another produces a deployment that boots and then refuses
10	//! at the first request that reads it, which is the worst place to find
11	//! out.
12	//!
13	//! This is the source, and `sesame-worker`'s config parser is held to it
14	//! mechanically: a test there scans its own source for `SESAME_*`
15	//! literals and asserts the two sets agree in both directions, so a name
16	//! rostered and never read fails, and a name read and never rostered
17	//! fails. The three configuration files are not yet held to it; holding
18	//! them is the deploy tooling's own job and lands with it.
19	//!
20	//! # Why the whole crate has no dependencies by default
21	//!
22	//! `sesame-worker` compiles to wasm and a dependency here is a
23	//! dependency in the bundle. Everything past the roster (the stage
24	//! grammar, the plan, the renders) sits behind the `plan` feature, which
25	//! only `sesame-cli` enables.
26	
27	/// What a binding is, which decides where its value comes from and
28	/// whether it may ever be printed.
29	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
30	pub enum BindingKind {
31	    /// A plain `[vars]` entry: a policy number, a URL, a word. Safe in a
32	    /// rendered config, a log, and a pull request.
33	    Var,
34	    /// A secret binding, pushed through `wrangler secret put` and never
35	    /// written to disk or rendered. Its value never leaves the operator's
36	    /// shell (CLAUDE.md §5).
37	    Secret,
38	    /// A platform binding rather than a value: a Hyperdrive connection,
39	    /// a send_email address. The deploy tooling wires it; no env carries
40	    /// it.
41	    Platform,
42	}
43	
44	/// Whether a deployment must carry the binding.
45	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
46	pub enum Requirement {
47	    /// Every deployment carries it, and config parse fails without it.
48	    Required,
49	    /// A deployment may omit it, and omitting it turns a surface off
50	    /// (ADR 0006's absent-config law).
51	    Optional,
52	    /// The grammar computes it from `(instance, stage)` and the origin,
53	    /// so an operator who sets it explicitly is overriding a derivation
54	    /// and the plan refuses.
55	    Derived,
56	}
57	
58	/// One binding.
59	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
60	pub struct Binding {
61	    /// The name, spelled exactly as every home spells it.
62	    pub name: &'static str,
63	    /// Where its value comes from.
64	    pub kind: BindingKind,
65	    /// Whether a deployment must carry it.
66	    pub requirement: Requirement,
67	    /// One line an operator reads in the rendered variable table.
68	    pub summary: &'static str,
69	}

539	//! The stage grammar: `(instance, stage)` in, every derived name out.
540	//!
541	//! Pure by construction. No I/O, no clock, no randomness, no ambient
542	//! environment read, which is CLAUDE.md §3's seam law applied to
543	//! deployment configuration: the same pair produces the same names on
544	//! any machine, so a plan is reviewable before it runs.
545	//!
546	//! No code path here compares a stage name to a literal outside
547	//! [`Stage::parse`]. Behavior derives from the env map; names derive from
548	//! the pair. That separation is what keeps "which stage is this" from
549	//! spreading into every derivation.
550	
551	use crate::error::DeployError;
552	
553	use core::fmt;
554	
555	/// The instance name's shape: a lowercase word, two to twenty-five
556	/// characters. It is the only free-form half of the pair.
557	const INSTANCE_MIN: usize = 2;
558	const INSTANCE_MAX: usize = 25;
559	
560	/// The stage vocabulary, parsed rather than pattern-matched.
561	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
562	pub enum Stage {
563	    /// The live deployment.
564	    Production,
565	    /// The proving ground main deploys to.
566	    Staging,
567	    /// One pull request's own deployment, destroyed when it closes.
568	    Preview(u32),
569	}
570	
571	impl Stage {
572	    /// Parses a stage word.
573	    ///
574	    /// # Errors
575	    /// [`DeployError::UnknownStage`] for anything outside the vocabulary.
576	    /// The vocabulary is closed on purpose: a typo that produced a fourth
577	    /// stage would deploy a real worker under a name nothing sweeps.
578	    pub fn parse(raw: &str) -> Result<Self, DeployError> {
579	        match raw {
580	            "production" => Ok(Self::Production),
581	            "staging" => Ok(Self::Staging),
582	            other => {
583	                let number = other
584	                    .strip_prefix("preview-")
585	                    .and_then(|digits| digits.parse::<u32>().ok())
586	                    .filter(|number| *number > 0);
587	                number.map(Self::Preview).ok_or(DeployError::UnknownStage)
588	            }
589	        }
590	    }
591	
592	    /// The stage's own word, which is also its suffix.
593	    ///
594	    /// why every stage carries a suffix, production included: the
595	    /// deployment id joins the instance and the stage, and without a
596	    /// suffix on production the join stops being injective. With one,
597	    /// (`acme`, `production`) gives `sesame-acme-production` and
598	    /// (`acme-production`, anything) can only ever be longer.
599	    #[must_use]
600	    pub fn word(self) -> String {
601	        match self {
602	            Self::Production => "production".to_owned(),
603	            Self::Staging => "staging".to_owned(),
604	            Self::Preview(number) => format!("preview-{number}"),
605	        }
606	    }
607	
608	    /// The GitHub environment this stage deploys under, which is what
609	    /// carries production's reviewer gate.
610	    #[must_use]
611	    pub const fn github_environment(self) -> &'static str {
612	        match self {
613	            Self::Production => "production",
614	            Self::Staging => "staging",
615	            Self::Preview(_) => "preview",
616	        }
617	    }

654	    ///
655	    /// # Errors
656	    /// [`DeployError::BadInstance`] when the instance is outside its
657	    /// shape, and [`DeployError::UnknownStage`] for a stage outside the
658	    /// vocabulary.
659	    pub fn new(instance: &str, stage: &str) -> Result<Self, DeployError> {
660	        let stage = Stage::parse(stage)?;
661	        if !(INSTANCE_MIN..=INSTANCE_MAX).contains(&instance.len()) {
662	            return Err(DeployError::BadInstance);
663	        }
664	        let mut bytes = instance.bytes();
665	        let Some(first) = bytes.next() else {
666	            return Err(DeployError::BadInstance);
667	        };
668	        if !first.is_ascii_lowercase() {
669	            return Err(DeployError::BadInstance);
670	        }
671	        if !bytes.all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_lowercase() || byte.is_ascii_digit() || byte == b'-') {
672	            return Err(DeployError::BadInstance);
673	        }
674	        if instance.ends_with('-') || instance.contains("--") {
675	            return Err(DeployError::BadInstance);
676	        }
677	        // why this one refusal by name: an operator who writes
678	        // `sesame-acme` gets `sesame-sesame-acme-production`, which
679	        // works, deploys, and reads as a mistake forever after. Refusing
680	        // it here costs one line and saves a rename.
681	        if instance.starts_with("sesame-") || instance == "sesame" {
682	            return Err(DeployError::InstanceIsPrefixed);
683	        }
684	        Ok(Self {
685	            instance: instance.to_owned(),
686	            stage,
687	        })
688	    }

899	//! The environment map: the small set of secrets and ids the grammar
900	//! reads, behind a type rather than an ambient `std::env` call.
901	//!
902	//! CLAUDE.md §3's seam law says the core reads no ambient environment,
903	//! and a deployment plan is exactly the kind of thing that should be
904	//! reproducible from stated inputs. The caller builds the map; the
905	//! grammar reads it. That is what makes a plan an artifact a reviewer can
906	//! read before anything runs, rather than something only reproducible on
907	//! the machine that produced it.

918	/// value that becomes a worker binding keeps its binding name everywhere,
919	/// so `.dev.vars`, `image/serve.mjs`, `workerd/rig.ts`, and the fleet
920	/// environment all spell `SESAME_ENVELOPE_KEK` the same way. This prefix
921	/// marks the values that never become bindings at all.
922	pub const DEPLOY_PREFIX: &str = "SESAME_DEPLOY_";

933	/// A read-only view of the environment the plan derives from.
934	///
935	/// `BTreeMap` rather than a hash: the plan renders in a stable order, and
936	/// a stable order is what makes a plan diffable between two runs.
937	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
938	pub struct EnvMap(BTreeMap<String, String>);

940	impl EnvMap {
941	    /// Builds a map from pairs.
942	    ///
943	    /// # Examples
944	    /// ```
945	    /// use sesame_deploy::env::{EnvMap, ORIGIN};
946	    /// let env = EnvMap::from_pairs([(ORIGIN, "https://auth.acme.com")]);
947	    /// assert_eq!(env.get(ORIGIN), Some("https://auth.acme.com"));
948	    /// ```
949	    #[must_use]
950	    pub fn from_pairs<K, V, I>(pairs: I) -> Self
951	    where
952	        I: IntoIterator<Item = (K, V)>,
953	        K: Into<String>,
954	        V: Into<String>,
955	    {
956	        Self(
957	            pairs
958	                .into_iter()
959	                .map(|(key, value)| (key.into(), value.into()))
960	                // An empty value is an absent value, matching the
961	                // worker's own optional reader: a blank binding is how
962	                // the lane turns a surface off, and the two halves must
963	                // agree on that or a rendered config would enable a
964	                // surface the worker then refuses.
965	                .filter(|(_, value): &(String, String)| !value.is_empty())
966	                .collect(),
967	        )
968	    }
969	
970	    /// Reads one name.
971	    #[must_use]
972	    pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
973	        self.0.get(name).map(String::as_str)
974	    }
975	
976	    /// Whether a name is present.
977	    #[must_use]
978	    pub fn has(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
979	        self.0.contains_key(name)
980	    }
981	
982	    /// Every name present, in stable order.
983	    pub fn names(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
984	        self.0.keys().map(String::as_str)

1016	//! The deploy grammar's closed error taxonomy.
1017	//!
1018	//! Every variant names a shape the operator got wrong, and none of them
1019	//! carries a value from the environment map. That is not politeness: the
1020	//! env map holds a database password and two 32-byte secrets, and an
1021	//! error type that could carry one would eventually print one into a CI
1022	//! log. The property lane asserts it over arbitrary maps.
1023	
1024	use core::fmt;
1025	
1026	/// Why a deployment plan could not be built.
1027	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
1028	pub enum DeployError {
1029	    /// The instance name is outside its shape.
1030	    BadInstance,
1031	    /// The instance name already carries the `sesame-` prefix the
1032	    /// deployment id adds.
1033	    InstanceIsPrefixed,
1034	    /// The stage word is outside the closed vocabulary.
1035	    UnknownStage,
1036	    /// A required variable is absent. The field name is static text from
1037	    /// the roster, never a value.
1038	    Missing(&'static str),
1039	    /// A present variable's shape is wrong. Again, the name only.
1040	    Malformed(&'static str),
1041	    /// A variable the grammar derives was set explicitly. Setting it is
1042	    /// an operator overriding a derivation, which the plan refuses rather
1043	    /// than silently preferring one of the two.
1044	    Derived(&'static str),
1045	    /// Half of a both-or-neither pair is present.
1046	    HalfPair(&'static str),
1047	}
1048	
1049	impl fmt::Display for DeployError {
1050	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
1051	        match self {
1052	            Self::BadInstance => f.write_str(
1053	                "the instance is a lowercase word of 2 to 25 characters, \
1054	                 starting with a letter, with single hyphens inside",
1055	            ),
1056	            Self::InstanceIsPrefixed => {
1057	                f.write_str("the instance carries no sesame- prefix: the deployment id adds it")
1058	            }
1059	            Self::UnknownStage => {
1060	                f.write_str("the stage is production, staging, or preview-<number>")
1061	            }
1062	            Self::Missing(name) => write!(f, "{name} is required and absent"),
1063	            Self::Malformed(name) => write!(f, "{name} is present and malformed"),
1064	            Self::Derived(name) => write!(
1065	                f,
1066	                "{name} is derived from the deployment's origin; remove it"
1067	            ),
1068	            Self::HalfPair(name) => write!(f, "{name} needs its other half"),
1069	        }
1070	    }
1071	}

1082	//! Rendering the roster as a Markdown table an operator reads.
1083	//!
1084	//! Generated rather than written, because a hand-written table drifts
1085	//! from the roster the moment a binding lands, and the drift stays
1086	//! invisible until an operator follows the table and gets a deployment
1087	//! that refuses at its first request. The golden lane pins these bytes,
1088	//! so a roster change shows up as a table change in the same diff.
1089	
1090	use core::fmt::Write as _;
1091	
1092	use crate::roster::{Binding, BindingKind, Requirement, BINDINGS};
1093	
1094	/// Renders every binding as one Markdown table.
1095	///
1096	/// # Examples
1097	/// ```
1098	/// let table = sesame_deploy::render::table::render();
1099	/// assert!(table.starts_with("| Name | Kind |"));
1100	/// assert!(table.contains("SESAME_ENVELOPE_KEK"));
1101	/// ```
1102	#[must_use]
1103	pub fn render() -> String {
1104	    let mut out = String::from("| Name | Kind | Required | What |\n|---|---|---|---|\n");
1105	    for binding in BINDINGS {
1106	        // why the ignored result: the sink is a String, which cannot fail
1107	        // to accept bytes. `write!` over `push_str(&format!(..))` avoids
1108	        // the intermediate allocation per row.
1109	        let _ = writeln!(
1110	            out,
1111	            "| `{}` | {} | {} | {} |",
1112	            binding.name,
1113	            kind_word(binding),
1114	            requirement_word(binding),
1115	            binding.summary
1116	        );
1117	    }
1118	    out
1119	}
1120	
1121	/// The kind's word for a reader rather than for a compiler.
1122	fn kind_word(binding: &Binding) -> &'static str {
1123	    match binding.kind {
1124	        BindingKind::Var => "var",
1125	        BindingKind::Secret => "secret",
1126	        BindingKind::Platform => "platform",
1127	    }
1128	}
1129	
1130	/// The requirement's word.
1131	fn requirement_word(binding: &Binding) -> &'static str {
1132	    match binding.requirement {
1133	        Requirement::Required => "yes",
1134	        Requirement::Optional => "no",
1135	        Requirement::Derived => "derived",
1136	    }
1137	}

1140	//! Rendering a plan as `wrangler.toml`.
1141	//!
1142	//! This is the self-hoster's path. A deployment that runs on the fleet
1143	//! goes through alchemy, which reads the plan's JSON; a deployment that
1144	//! runs anywhere else needs a file `wrangler deploy` understands, and
1145	//! this writes it from the same plan, so the two paths cannot drift into
1146	//! different deployments of the same product.
1147	//!
1148	//! Secrets never appear. The rendered file names them in a comment so the
1149	//! operator knows which `wrangler secret put` calls follow, and carries
1150	//! none of their values: this file lands on disk and in a git repository.
1151	
1152	use core::fmt::Write as _;
1153	
1154	use crate::plan::DeployPlan;

1156	/// Renders the plan.
1157	///
1158	/// # Examples
1159	/// ```

1161	/// # use sesame_deploy::{plan, render::wrangler};
1162	/// # fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
1163	/// # use sesame_deploy::roster::{self, BindingKind, Requirement};
1164	/// # // Every required var, filled: a deployment names all of them, and
1165	/// # // the plan refuses by name until it does.
1166	/// # let mut pairs: Vec<(String, String)> = roster::of_kind(BindingKind::Var)
1167	/// #     .filter(|binding| binding.requirement == Requirement::Required)
1168	/// #     .map(|binding| (binding.name.to_owned(), "1000".to_owned()))
1169	/// #     .collect();
1170	/// # pairs.push((ORIGIN.to_owned(), "https://auth.acme.com".to_owned()));
1171	/// # pairs.push(("SESAME_ENVELOPE_KEK".to_owned(), "kek".to_owned()));
1172	/// # pairs.push(("SESAME_PEPPER".to_owned(), "pepper".to_owned()));
1173	/// # let env = EnvMap::from_pairs(pairs);
1174	/// let rendered = wrangler::render(&plan("acme", "production", &env)?);
1175	/// assert!(rendered.contains(r#"name = "sesame-acme-production""#));
1176	/// // No secret value can be here, because the plan never carried one.
1177	/// assert!(!rendered.contains("SESAME_PEPPER ="));

1179	/// # }

1183	    // why every write's result is ignored: the sink is a String, which
1184	    // cannot fail to accept bytes.
1185	    let mut out = String::new();
1186	    let _ = writeln!(
1187	        out,
1188	        "# Generated from the deployment pair ({}, {}) by sesame's own\n\
1189	         # deployment grammar. Every value here derives from that pair and\n\
1190	         # this deployment's environment; editing the file by hand puts it\n\
1191	         # out of step with the grammar that renders it again.\n",
1192	        plan.instance, plan.stage,
1193	    );
1194	    let _ = writeln!(out, "name = \"{}\"", plan.worker.name);
1195	    out.push_str("main = \"build/worker/index.js\"\n");
1196	    let _ = writeln!(
1197	        out,
1198	        "compatibility_date = \"{}\"",
1199	        plan.worker.compatibility_date
1200	    );
1201	    out.push_str("compatibility_flags = [\"nodejs_compat\"]\n\n");
1202	
1203	    match &plan.worker.domain {
1204	        Some(domain) => {
1205	            out.push_str(
1206	                "# The custom domain, taken from the deployment's own origin. The zone\n\
1207	                 # must already exist in this Cloudflare account.\n",

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The docs/testing/lanes.toml table, the lane docs in docs/testing/, and the
# lane jobs in .github/workflows/ci.yml are a bijection (CLAUDE.md §8). This
# script fails the build on drift in any direction: a row without a doc, a
# doc without a row, a lane without a job, or a job that runs nothing. The
# contract it pins: lane id equals job id equals doc basename.
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C

ROOT="${1:-.}"
cd "$ROOT"
TABLE="docs/testing/lanes.toml"
CI=".github/workflows/ci.yml"

lanes="$(grep -oE '^\[lane\.[a-z0-9-]+\]$' "$TABLE" | sed -E 's/^\[lane\.([a-z0-9-]+)\]$/\1/' | sort)"
docs="$(find docs/testing -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' -exec basename {} .md \; | sort)"

rowless="$(comm -13 <(printf '%s\n' "$lanes") <(printf '%s\n' "$docs"))"
if [ -n "$rowless" ]; then
  echo "lane docs with no table row (add the [lane.<id>] row or remove the doc):"
  printf '%s\n' "$rowless"
  exit 1
fi

docless="$(comm -23 <(printf '%s\n' "$lanes") <(printf '%s\n' "$docs"))"
if [ -n "$docless" ]; then
  echo "table rows with no lane doc (write docs/testing/<id>.md in the same commit):"
  printf '%s\n' "$docless"
  exit 1
fi

# Lanes run as jobs in ci.yml; the integration lane runs after staging
# deploys in deploy.yml, because its subject exists only there. A lane's
# home moves; it never leaves the bijection.
JOBFILES=("$CI")
[ -f .github/workflows/deploy.yml ] && JOBFILES+=(.github/workflows/deploy.yml)

jobs="$(awk '
  /^jobs:[[:space:]]*$/ { injobs = 1; next }
  injobs && /^[^ ]/ { injobs = 0 }
  injobs && /^  [a-z0-9-]+:$/ {
    name = $1
    sub(/:$/, "", name)
    print name
  }
' "${JOBFILES[@]}" | sort -u)"

jobless="$(comm -23 <(printf '%s\n' "$lanes") <(printf '%s\n' "$jobs"))"
if [ -n "$jobless" ]; then
  echo "lanes with no CI job (the lane lands when its job runs; add the job or drop the row):"
  printf '%s\n' "$jobless"
  exit 1
fi

for lane in $lanes; do
  lane_found=0
  for jobfile in "${JOBFILES[@]}"; do
    if awk -v lane="$lane" '
      $0 == "  " lane ":" { inlane = 1; next }
      inlane && /^  [a-z0-9-]+:$/ { inlane = 0 }
      inlane && $0 ~ "just +" lane "([[:space:]]|$)" { found = 1 }
      END { exit !found }
    ' "$jobfile"; then
      lane_found=1
      break
    fi
  done
  if [ "$lane_found" -ne 1 ]; then
    echo "lane $lane has no job anywhere that runs 'just $lane'"
    exit 1
  fi
done

47	   the daily one (`M H * * *`) and reports the period of each. Every
48	   other cron expression still answers nothing, so a console shows no
49	   countdown rather than a wrong one.

# ADR 0019: The collector fires hourly, and health measures against that

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-09-08
- **Context doc:** [0005-gc-on-the-cron.md](0005-gc-on-the-cron.md);
  [../DEPLOY.md](../DEPLOY.md)

## Context

ADR 0005 gave the collector one firing a day and a per-invocation budget
of 900 binding operations, with runs that park a cursor and resume on the
next firing. Those two decisions interact in a way the original record
did not work through.

Before the sweep can delete a candidate's NAR, the collect stage has to
learn which NAR the candidate's narinfo names, and that is one bucket
read per candidate. A run plans nothing until it has collected every
candidate, so the reads a deployment can afford per day have to exceed
the paths that cross the grace window per day. One firing a day meant
about 860 reads after the listing and the mark stage took their share.

Production crossed that line on 8 September 2026, the first day anything
was old enough to sweep. The 14-day window expired on roughly 4,900
paths at once. The run collected 534 of them, parked, and waited for the
next day, while another day's worth of paths kept crossing the window at
over a thousand a day. The candidate set was growing faster than the
collector could read it, so no run would ever reach its sweep. Fourteen
runs had already deleted nothing, and the inventory had gone from 4,966
narinfos to 14,634.

The health route had a related problem, invisible until the schedule
changed. Its staleness bound was two days, written as a constant rather
than derived from the cron, so it happened to mean two cron periods
only while the cron was daily.

## Decision

1. The cron is `0 * * * *`. Twenty-four firings a day multiply the
   collect stage's daily allowance by twenty-four and change no single
   invocation's ceiling, so nothing about the per-run budget, the
   resumability, or the gates moves.
2. Health's staleness bound is two of the deployment's own cron periods,
   read from `CACHET_GC_CRON` through the schedule parser. A cron the
   parser does not recognize falls back to two days, which is the loose
   answer rather than one guessed from an expression nobody read.
3. The schedule parser recognizes the hourly shape (`M * * * *`) beside
   the daily one (`M H * * *`) and reports the period of each. Every
   other cron expression still answers nothing, so a console shows no
   countdown rather than a wrong one.
4. Health reads `meta/gc-cursor` and treats a parked run as proof the
   schedule fired. Reports land only when a run concludes, so a
   collection spanning many ticks leaves the newest report aging while
   the collector works, and with an hourly bound that would answer
   `degraded` during ordinary operation.

## Consequences

A deployment collects on the hour. A tick with nothing to do spends its
listing and exits, so the added firings cost a bucket listing an hour on
an idle cache. Production's 4,900-path backlog drains in about six
firings instead of never.

The colour on the console now means something on both schedules: an
hourly deployment goes `degraded` after two missed hours, where it used
to need two days of silence, which is forty-eight missed firings.

Health costs one more bucket read per request. It is an admin route the
console polls, and the read is a `get` on one small key.

## Alternatives considered

**Raise `GC_OP_BUDGET`.** More reads per firing rather than more
firings. Rejected: the budget exists to keep one invocation inside the
platform's subrequest and CPU ceilings, and raising it trades a
collector that cannot finish for invocations that get killed partway.

**Bound the collect stage instead: plan and sweep what has been
collected so far.** This converges without touching the cron, and it is
the more thorough fix, because it removes the requirement that one run
see every candidate. Rejected for now: partial plans mean a NAR whose
narinfo was collected in one run and swept in another, and working out
which orderings stay safe is a larger change than the schedule that was
starving it. Worth doing if the read per candidate ever becomes the
bottleneck again.

**Store each narinfo's NAR key beside it at write time** so the collect
stage needs no read at all. The measurement written when a NAR lands
(ADR 0012) is the natural place. This is the real fix to the cost and
not just to the allowance, and it stays open.

1	# ADR 0011: Deployments are named, and the name is housekeeping
2	
3	- **Status:** Accepted
4	- **Date:** 2026-08-21
5	- **Context doc:** [../DEPLOY.md](../DEPLOY.md); supersedes the stage
6	  grammar of [ADR 0009](0009-alchemy-deployments.md) (its isolation and
7	  idempotence decisions stand)
8	
9	## Context
10	
11	cachet is self-hosted: every operator runs their own deployments, and an
12	operator may run several in one account (a staging rehearsal, multiple
13	production caches for different orgs). ADR 0009 framed stages as the
14	fixed pair `staging`/`production` and special-cased production:
15	only it defaulted its domain to the host, every other stage refused
16	without `CACHET_DEPLOY_DOMAIN`, and GC grace defaulted by stage name.
17	When deployments became a user-facing concept, the fixed pair could not
18	express "four production deployments in this account", and the
19	name-keyed special cases pushed deploy behavior into string comparisons.
20	
21	## Decision
22	
23	1. A deployment has an operator-chosen name matching
24	   `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, asked for first at `just bootstrap`. The
25	   name drives the env file (`infra/.env.<name>`), the alchemy stage,
26	   and the resource names (`cachet-<name>`; the prefix is a guarantee,
27	   not a ritual — a name already starting with `cachet-` is used as-is,
28	   so no stack ever reads `cachet-cachet-*`). `infra/src/config.ts`
29	   enforces the grammar on every deploy, so hand-written env files obey
30	   it too.
31	2. The name is housekeeping. The protocol identity stays the host: the
32	   signing key is `<host>-1`, narinfo signatures name hosts, and
33	   renaming a deployment never re-signs anything.
34	3. The custom domain defaults to the host for every deployment;
35	   `CACHET_DEPLOY_DOMAIN` is a pure override. The production-only
36	   default and the no-domain refusal are deleted.
37	4. GC grace defaults to the worker's fourteen days for every deployment;
38	   throwaway deployments opt into zero explicitly through
39	   `CACHET_DEPLOY_GC_GRACE_MS`. This repository's own staging pins the
40	   zero in its deploy workflow, where the reason is readable.
41	5. One name converges one stack per account: two operators sharing an
42	   account who both deploy `production` run one shared stack. DEPLOY.md
43	   carries the caveat.
44	
45	## Consequences
46	
47	`just deploy <name>` and `just destroy <name>` need no other changes:
48	recipes were already parameterized, and bootstrap now owns naming.
49	Account-side state (ADR 0009's decision) is keyed by stage, so each
50	name keeps its own state rows and upgrades or destroys one deployment
51	without touching another. Bootstrap's rerun path doubles as recovery:
52	the non-secret values regenerate from the live deployment's public
53	config, and only the two secrets need a second copy kept (password
54	manager or the CI environment), with rotation as the floor.
55	
56	## Alternatives considered
57	
58	Keep the fixed `staging`/`production` pair and let extra deployments be
59	forks: multiplies review surface for a naming problem; rejected. Make
60	the deployment name part of the signing identity (`<name>-<host>-1`):
61	renaming a deployment would rotate client trust for zero protocol
62	benefit, since signatures answer "which cache signed this", not "which
63	stack"; rejected. Require `CACHET_DEPLOY_DOMAIN` on every non-production
64	name (the old rule, generalized): one more first-deploy failure mode
65	that the host already answers; rejected.
66

name = "cachet-deploy"
description = "The deployment grammar: the binding roster the worker imports, the name grammar, the secret-free plan, and the release manifest. No I/O, no clock, no ambient environment."
edition.workspace = true
version.workspace = true
publish.workspace = true
license.workspace = true

workspace = true

[features]
default = ["plan"]
# why default-on with the worker opting out, rather than default-off: the
# property and golden lanes reach this crate with a plain
# `--workspace --test <name>`, and a default-off feature would leave them
# silently not compiling the tests at all, which is the failure CLAUDE.md
# §9 exists to prevent. The worker sets default-features = false, so the
# roster it imports brings no dependency into the wasm bundle.
plan = ["dep:serde", "dep:serde_json"]

serde = { workspace = true, optional = true }
serde_json = { workspace = true, optional = true }

hegeltest.workspace = true

# as JSON snapshots keeps a diff readable as a diff of the document.
insta = { workspace = true, features = ["json"] }

# action with its own binary, the way cachet-api's openapi binary is.
[[bin]]
name = "deploy-manifest"
path = "src/bin/deploy_manifest.rs"
required-features = ["plan"]

2	//! the deployer.
3	//!
4	//! A manifest describes one release of cachet as a template. Every
5	//! account-specific value is a placeholder from a closed set, and a
6	//! deployer renders the placeholders from an instance's own state before
7	//! it touches an account. The template alone is `deploy-manifest.json` at
8	//! the repository root, committed and drift-gated; the release workflow
9	//! adds the measured artifacts (module hashes, the asset map) and signs
10	//! the result.
11	//!
12	//! The placeholders:
13	//!
14	//! | Placeholder | Meaning |
15	//! | --- | --- |
16	//! | `$NAME` | the deployment's name as the operator wrote it |
17	//! | `$RESOURCE_NAME` | `cachet-<name>`, or the name when already prefixed |
18	//! | `$RESOURCE_NAME_UNDERSCORED` | the same with dashes as underscores |
19	//! | `$HOST` | the cache's host |
20	//! | `$VAR(<binding>)` | the operator's value for a var |
21	//! | `$SECRET(<binding>)` | the operator's value for a secret, never rendered into anything printable |
22	//! | `$VERSION` | this release's version |
23	//! | `$GENERATED_PUBLIC(<secret>)` | the public half of a key the deployer generated for a secret |

86	/// added here because a plan should refuse a typo the platform would
87	/// otherwise refuse later with a worse message: a grace window that is

92	/// variant carries a value from `env`, only names.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The deploy-manifest bijection: cachet-deploy's roster and release
# constants against the committed deploy-manifest.json, which is what a
# deployer reads. This script regenerates the document and fails the build
# on any drift, because the contract a deployer renders and the code must
# be one fact (CLAUDE.md §0).
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="${1:-.}"
cd "$ROOT"

regenerated="$(mktemp -t cachet-deploy-manifest.XXXXXX)"
trap 'rm -f "$regenerated"' EXIT

cargo run --quiet -p cachet-deploy --bin deploy-manifest >"$regenerated"

if ! cmp -s deploy-manifest.json "$regenerated"; then
  echo "deploy-manifest.json drifts from the deployment grammar."
  echo "Regenerate it: nix develop --command just deploy-manifest"
  diff -u deploy-manifest.json "$regenerated" | head -50 || true
  exit 1
fi

echo "deploy-manifest.json is in step with the code."

# Every recipe is a thin alias over a flake output; the build logic lives in
# the flake, never here. `just check` is the pre-push parity verb: green
# locally means green in CI, because CI runs the same verbs.

sys := `nix eval --impure --raw --expr 'builtins.currentSystem'`

default: check

# the pre-push parity verb: every gate, one to one with the CI jobs
check:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    gates="$(nix eval --json '.#checks.{{ sys }}' --apply 'builtins.attrNames' | jq -r '.[] | ".#checks.{{ sys }}." + .')"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    nix build -L --keep-going $gates
    just deny
    just kani
    just wasm
    just clippy-wasm
    just wasm-hygiene
    just openapi-check

# format the tree
fmt:
    nix fmt

# check formatting
fmt-check:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.fmt'

# the workspace lint gate
clippy:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.clippy'

# the unit lane
unit:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.unit'

# the property lane
property:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.property'

# the golden lane
golden:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.golden'

# the kani lane; impure: the pinned verifier and its toolchain install under the user
kani crate="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    # why: kani-verifier is not packaged in nixpkgs; its pinned install and
    # toolchain download live outside the dev shell, like cargo deny.
    export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
    command -v cargo-kani >/dev/null 2>&1 || cargo install --locked kani-verifier@0.67.0
    cargo kani setup
    if [ -n "{{ crate }}" ]; then
        cargo kani -p "{{ crate }}"
    else
        for c in $(bash scripts/list-kani-crates.sh); do cargo kani -p "$c"; done
    fi

# the CLAUDE.md manifest bijection
doc-manifest:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.doc-manifest'

# the lane bijection
lane-manifest:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.lane-manifest'

# the workflow lint
actionlint:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.actionlint'

# the shell lint
scripts:
    nix build -L '.#checks.{{ sys }}.scripts'

# the impure gate: cargo deny fetches the advisory database
deny:
    cargo deny check

# regenerate docs/openapi.yaml from the route descriptors
openapi:
    cargo run -p cachet-api --features yaml-export --bin openapi > docs/openapi.yaml

# the OpenAPI bijection: descriptors against the committed document
openapi-check:
    bash scripts/check-openapi-drift.sh

# build the deployable worker bundle with worker-build, then stamp the JS
# loader with the wasm's hash: deploy-time drift detection hashes the
# entry, whose text worker-build emits identically on every build — the
# stamp is how wasm-only changes still read as a change (ADR 0009).
wasm:
    # The commit the bundle was built from, stamped into the binary so the
    # console's header names it. A build outside a git tree leaves it
    # empty, and the worker then says nothing rather than naming a commit
    # it was not built from.
    cd crates/cachet-worker && CACHET_BUILD_SHA="$(git rev-parse --short=6 HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo '')" worker-build --profile worker
    printf '// cachet-bundle-sha256: %s\n' "$(openssl dgst -sha256 -r crates/cachet-worker/build/index_bg.wasm | cut -d' ' -f1)" >> crates/cachet-worker/build/index.js

# build the browser console into web/dist, which the deploy uploads as
# the worker's static assets (ADR 0014)
web:
    cd web && bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run build

# the console lane: the console's pure derivations and its presentational
# components, under vitest (docs/testing/console.md)
console:
    cd web && bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run typecheck && bun run test

# the workerd lane: the built worker under wrangler dev --local, real R2
# and Cache API semantics, asserted over real HTTP; the CLI binary rides
# the same lane, driven by the end-to-end push scenario
workerd: wasm
    cargo build -p cachet-cli
    node workerd/check.mjs fixtures/nix-signed

# the shipped-artifact hygiene gate: no banned runtimes, no secret-shaped strings
wasm-hygiene:
    bash scripts/check-wasm-hygiene.sh

# the worker crate's own lint pass, on its production target (the host
# clippy gate excludes it because it is wasm32-only)
clippy-wasm:
    cargo clippy -p cachet-worker --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --all-features -- --deny warnings

# deploy one stage end to end: build the bundle, source the stage's env
# file when present, run the alchemy stack. The operator's two secrets and
# the CACHET_DEPLOY_* set come from infra/.env.<stage> or the environment.
deploy stage: wasm web
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cd infra
    bun install --frozen-lockfile --silent
    if [ -f ".env.{{ stage }}" ]; then
        set -a
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        . ".env.{{ stage }}"
        set +a
    fi

    # terminal cannot answer, so every CI deploy stopped at the prompt
    # with "Non-interactive terminal detected". Approving on behalf of a
    # run that has no way to be asked is not a decision being taken away
    # from anyone: it is the only answer available. A terminal still gets
    # the prompt, which is where a human is present to read the plan.
    approve=()

        approve=(--yes)
    fi

    # answers its own refusal with a zero exit, so a deploy that printed
    # its plan and applied none of it reported success: staging went green
    # for days while running whatever it had before, and the integration
    # lane behind it tested that stale worker and passed. A deploy that
    # deploys nothing has to be red.
    log="$(mktemp)"
    trap 'rm -f "${log}"' EXIT
    set +e
    bun run deploy --stage "{{ stage }}" "${approve[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "${log}"
    status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
    set -e
    if [ "${status}" -ne 0 ]; then
        exit "${status}"
    fi
    if grep -q "Non-interactive terminal detected" "${log}"; then
        echo "cachet: alchemy printed its plan and applied none of it." >&2
        echo "  The deployment is unchanged. Nothing here can answer its prompt," >&2
        echo "  so this run cannot deploy; it must not report that it did." >&2
        exit 1
    fi

# tear one stage down; alchemy confirms before deleting anything
destroy stage:

    cd infra
    if [ -f ".env.{{ stage }}" ]; then
        set -a
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        . ".env.{{ stage }}"
        set +a
    fi
    bun run destroy --stage "{{ stage }}"

# checklists for the GitHub and Cloudflare sides
bootstrap *args:
    bash scripts/bootstrap.sh {{ args }}

# the integration lane: the live round trip against a deployment
integration:
    bash scripts/integration.sh

# One job per gate, job id equal to gate name (scripts/check-lane-manifest.sh
# pins the lane half of this contract). Local parity is structural: CI runs
# `nix develop --command just <gate>`, the same verb a laptop runs.
name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

permissions:
  contents: read
  # The cachet action mints its read/write credential from the job's OIDC
  # token; jobs without the grant build uncached, by the action's design.
  id-token: write

jobs:
  fmt:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: nix on the cachet cache
        uses: nox-systems/cachet/action@v0
        with:
          cache-url: https://cachet.nox.so
          roots: .#devShells.x86_64-linux.default
      - run: nix develop --command just fmt-check

  clippy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: nix on the cachet cache
        uses: nox-systems/cachet/action@v0
        with:
          cache-url: https://cachet.nox.so
          roots: .#devShells.x86_64-linux.default
      - run: nix develop --command just clippy

  unit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: nix on the cachet cache
        uses: nox-systems/cachet/action@v0
        with:
          cache-url: https://cachet.nox.so
          roots: .#devShells.x86_64-linux.default
      - run: nix develop --command just unit

  property:

# CLAUDE.md: the cachet constitution

cachet is a self-hostable nix binary cache on Cloudflare Workers, written
in Rust with workers-rs. This document binds every contribution and every
agent that works in this repository. Every rule carries its reason.

## §0 The prime directive

A gate, lane, or doc name exists in conversation only when it exists in the
flake, the justfile, or the manifest. Suggesting a check that cannot run is
a defect. When you add one, land the verb, the CI job, and the doc row in
one commit.

## §1 The stack

The worker runs on workers-rs compiled to wasm32-unknown-unknown, with R2
as the only cache-data store and KV for auth verdicts, sessions, and
OAuth state only. Deployments are provisioned by an alchemy-run program
under `infra/`; the `cachet` CLI ships natively through cargo-dist; the
GitHub Action lives in this repo under `action/`. The browser console is
a React application in `web/`, built by `just web` and uploaded as the
worker's static assets. The three auth flows are GitHub OIDC for writes
and CI reads, GitHub device flow for laptop reads, and browser OAuth with
KV sessions for the console, whose sessions read the console's surface
and never the cache's contents. Signing is
server-side only, and a narinfo is signed only after its stored NAR
verifies byte-for-byte.

## §2 The prose law

PROSE.md governs every Markdown file, comment, and user-visible string in
this repository, including its own README. The doc-manifest gate enforces
that the manifest in §11 loads all of it.

## §3 Clock, entropy, and layout determinism

Time comes from a Clock seam sampled once at request start; entropy comes
from an Rng seam wired only at the worker edge; map layout uses BTreeMap
and BTreeSet. clippy.toml bans the ambient forms and the ban is
mechanical, not advisory. Banned verbatim: SystemTime::now, Instant::now,
thread::spawn, HashMap, HashSet.

## §4 Crate boundaries

The dependency direction is one-way: cachet-core is pure; cachet-crypto
computes; cachet-api describes the HTTP surface and generates the OpenAPI
document; cachet-worker is the wasm32 deployable that owns every binding;
cachet-push and cachet-cli are native writer tools; `web/` is the
console, which depends on the HTTP surface and on nothing in the
workspace. cachet-worker fails
host builds and is excluded from workspace default-members; its build and
its truth lane are the wasm verbs. A path dependency against this
direction fails review.

## §5 Wasm and crypto hygiene

aws-lc-rs, aws-lc-sys, and the C zstd crate do not build for
wasm32-unknown-unknown and are banned in deny.toml. ring shares the
incompatibility and is permitted only through the rustls chain
(deny.toml's wrappers), because the native crates need TLS on hosts and
rustls's provider choices are ring or aws-lc; every other path to ring
fails the gate. Hashing uses sha2, signing uses ed25519-dalek,
decompression uses ruzstd, and RS256 uses the crypto decided in docs/adr.
scripts/check-wasm-hygiene.sh scans the shipped bundle for the banned
runtimes and for secret-shaped strings; the gate protects the artifact,
not intentions.

## §6 Dependencies

Versions pin exactly where generation behavior matters and by minor series
elsewhere. New dependencies need one `// why:` comment at their
Cargo.toml entry: what they do and why nothing in the tree already does it.

## §7 Errors and panics

External-input failures are typed errors with the error-code table's
vocabulary; RFC 9457 problem+json bodies leave the worker. Invariant
violations panic with named invariants, and an attacker-reachable
condition never panics. Test code panics on missing fixtures rather than
skipping.

## §8 The manifest gates

Three bijections keep docs and runs honest, all enforced by scripts in
`scripts/`: the §11 manifest against the repo's non-ADR Markdown
(check-doc-manifest.sh), docs/testing/lanes.toml against the lane docs
and CI jobs (check-lane-manifest.sh), and cachet-api's route descriptors
against the committed docs/openapi.yaml (check-openapi-drift.sh).

## §9 The lanes

Every test belongs to exactly one lane, and each lane is job-named the
same everywhere: the lanes.toml row, the docs/testing doc, the just verb,
and the CI job. A failed test that passes on retry is a bug, never a flake:
retries stay zero. The registry docs/testing/lanes.toml is the list.

## §10 Comments

Code comments state why, not what: `// why:` begins every non-obvious
choice so the reason greps. Rustdoc states what a public item does; the
comment beside it states why the code chose this way.

## §11 Required context

The manifest below is the bijection's source. Scripts assert it loads
exactly the repo's non-ADR Markdown, no more and no less.

@PROSE.md
@SECURITY.md
@docs/DEPLOY.md
@docs/console.md
@docs/security/threat-model.md
@docs/testing/unit.md
@docs/testing/property.md
@docs/testing/golden.md
@docs/testing/kani.md
@docs/testing/console.md
@docs/testing/workerd.md
@docs/testing/integration.md

# cachet

cachet is a self-hostable nix binary cache that runs on Cloudflare Workers
and R2. One deployment serves the GitHub orgs you configure: CI pushes over an
OIDC-authenticated write path and the server signs each narinfo after
verifying its NAR byte-for-byte, laptops authenticate with GitHub device
flow, and garbage collection runs armed from the first day on a Cloudflare
cron. The repo holds the worker, the cachet CLI, a GitHub Action for CI
pushes, and the alchemy program that deploys it all into your own
Cloudflare account.

The easiest way to run your own: clone this repo, run `just bootstrap`
inside `nix develop`, and follow the printed checklists (the runbook is
[docs/DEPLOY.md](docs/DEPLOY.md).

## For laptop users

Install the CLI and wire the cache:

```
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf \
  'https://github.com/nox-systems/cachet/releases/latest/download/cachet-cli-installer.sh' | sh
cachet login --cache-url https://<the deployment's host>
cachet setup
cachet doctor
```

`login` signs in through GitHub and trades that identity for a
credential the deployment issues, good for thirty days; run it again to
renew, and `cachet logout` to revoke it. `setup` edits the daemon's
netrc and `/etc/nix/nix.custom.conf` and restarts the daemon. `doctor`
probes the wiring and prints what holds.

Several caches work at once. Tokens are kept per host, the netrc keeps
one block per host, and the substituter list accumulates, so logging in
and setting up against a second deployment leaves the first alone. Pass
`--cache-url` to name which one a command means; without it, commands
use the one you logged into last. Different deployments can be different
GitHub accounts.

Both nix installs work. On a machine running Determinate Nix, `setup`
registers the credential the way Determinate's daemon reads it and
restarts through `determinate-nixd`; on plain nix it writes `netrc-file`
and restarts through systemd or launchd. It detects which one the machine
has and names it in its output, so you do not have to know beforehand.

## For CI

In a workflow of any repo in the served org:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v7
  - uses: nox-systems/cachet/action@v0
    with:
      cache-url: https://<the deployment's host>
      roots: |
        .#my-package
```

The action installs nix trusting the cache, snapshots the store before
your build, and pushes what the build added on success. Signing happens
server-side; the job needs no secrets beyond its OIDC token.

## For admins

Open `https://<the deployment's host>/` in a browser and sign in with
GitHub. The console shows what the collector has been doing, what the
counters recorded, and who can reach the cache; it writes nothing. Admins

list sees the access screen alone. A browser session reads the console
and cannot substitute from the cache.

- `crates/`: the workspace. `cachet-core` (pure domain), `cachet-crypto`,
  `cachet-api` (the HTTP surface and the generated OpenAPI document),

- `action/`: the composite GitHub Action consumers wire into CI.
- `web/`: the browser console the deployment serves at `/console`.
- `infra/`: the alchemy stack that provisions a deployment.
- `docs/`: DEPLOY.md (the runbook), security/threat-model.md,

# The unit lane

The unit lane runs `cargo nextest` over the whole workspace except
cachet-worker, under the ci profile with zero retries (`.config/nextest.toml`).

parsers, document round-trips, claim-policy decisions, and the rejection
matrix. It exists to catch logic, parsing, and state-machine bugs close to
the code that has them.

coverage belongs to the golden lane. A test that fails intermittently is a
determinism bug in the code or the test, and the fix is never a retry
(CLAUDE.md §9).
